Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size, randomly connected hidden layer called the "reservoir," which processes the input data. The weights of the reservoir are typically fixed, and only the output weights are trained. Reservoirs in ESNs are often trained using random connectivity to ensure that they can capture a wide range of temporal dynamics. 

To summarize, ESNs use a large, randomly connected hidden layer to process time series data, with only the output weights being trained. This approach allows ESNs to be trained more efficiently than traditional recurrent neural networks.
